minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 24, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:04 p.m., on January 24, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 19, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  Council Member Raths

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Threat to Public Services or Facilities. Consultation with Orange County Sheriff’s
  Department – Chief of Mission Viejo Police Services and Captain; City of Mission
  Viejo Emergency Operations Manager; City of Mission Viejo Cyber Security/Video
  Operations Manager; City Attorney.

CS2. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One Matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9 (Case 34-2016-80002311).

City Council Minutes  1  January 24, 2017
 CS3. Conference with Real Property Negotiators. Property: APN 808-720-07, APN 808-
  571-01, APN 808-720-08, APN 808-720-09, APN 808-720-10, APN 808-720-11, APN
  808-720-12, APN 808-132-16. Agency Negotiators: City Manager Wilberg; Assistant
  City Manager Rattay; Community Development Director Lister; Administrative
  Services Director Dyas, City Attorney. Negotiating Parties: NGP Realty. Under
  Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that for item CS1, the City Council received reports but no
reportable action occurred. For item CS3, direction was given to the City's negotiators but no
reportable action occurred. City Attorney Curley noted that the Council did not consider item CS2
and it will be heard at a future City Council Meeting.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize the 2016 Employees of the Year

  Mayor Bucknum presented plaques to (1) Information Technology Specialist, Mark Joson,
  City of Mission Viejo Employee of the Year; (2) Deputy Joseph Cislo, Orange County
  Sheriff's Department Employee of the Year; and (3) Firefighter Tim Brooks, Orange
  County Fire Authority Employee of the Year.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Doug Zielasko, M.V.: introduced himself as the newly appointed executive of the Mission Viejo
Chamber of Commerce.

Sharon Cody: discussed problems with aggressive dogs and the overuse of La Paws Dog Park.
She suggested issuing permits to use the park and limiting the membership to residents of those
cities that contract with the Mission Viejo animal shelter.

Alison Edwards, representing OC Human Relations: reported on the work that OC Human
Relations has done in the City of Mission Viejo over the past year and she thanked the City for its
support.

Arnie Lynn Bengo, representing Working Wardrobes: stated that Working Wardrobes provides
career training, job placement assistance and professional wardrobe services for veterans so they
can be successful in the workforce. They are hosting a 5k Walk and Fun Run on Saturday, March
25, 2017, on the Oso Creek Trail and she asked the City to help promote the needs of veterans in
the community.
City Council Minutes  2  January 24, 2017
 Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: discussed the City's lawsuit against her for illegal parking of an RV at her
home.

Paulina Finorio, M.V.: stated that improvement is needed in the environment around her
condominium and she asked if a gate could be installed to enclose her neighborhood.

Rostin Rastgou, M.V.: asked if the City is interested in joining a non-profit organization, based in
Hiroshima, Japan, called Mayor’s for Peace.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Raths

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of January 10, 2017, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register Dated December 23, 2016 in the Amount of $4,202,614.69

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated January 6, 2017 in the amount of $524,642.05

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Review and Approval of Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the 17-18 A-B
  Annual Fiscal Period of July 1, 2017, to June 30, 2018

  (1) Adopted Successor Agency Resolution No. 17-01 approving the Recognized
  Obligation Payment Schedule for the 17-18 A-B for the annual fiscal period of July 1,
  2017, to June 30, 2018, Subject to Submittal to and Review by the Oversight and by the
City Council Minutes  3  January 24, 2017
   Department of Finance under the Division 24, Part 1.85 of the California Health and Safety
  Code, and Authorizing the Posting and Transmittal Thereof; and (2) further, the
  Administrative Services Director, in consultation with legal counsel, shall be authorized to
  request and complete meet and confer session(s), if any, with the Department of Finance
  and authorized to make augmentations, modifications, additions or revisions as may be
  necessary or directed by the Department of Finance.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2016

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2016

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  November 2016

  Received and filed.

9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for November 2016

  Received and filed.

10.  Purchase Two Toyota Prius - Replacement Code Enforcement Vehicles

  (1) Awarded a Purchase Agreement for Two Toyota Prius to Santa Margarita Toyota Scion
  in an amount not to exceed $54,017.50; and (2) adopted Resolution 17-04, Amending the
  FY 2016/17 Budget to Appropriate Funds From the Construction and Recycling Diversion
  Deposit Forfeitures for the Purchase of Two Fleet Vehicles.

11.  Alicia Parkway and Marguerite Parkway Intersection Improvements (CIP 232) and
  Santa Margarita Parkway and Marguerite Parkway Intersection Improvements (CIP
  233)

  Authorized issuance of a purchase order to Advantec Consulting Engineers, Inc., in an
  amount not to exceed $114,940 for design engineering services for the subject projects.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

12.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report
City Council Minutes  4  January 24, 2017
 13.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Mayor Bucknum deferred the reports for items 12 and 13 to her Council Comments.

STAFF REPORTS

14.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update

  Fire Chief John Abel presented an update on the recent storms and the OCFA's resources
  and response.

15.  MV Shuttle Status Report

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the report.

  Michael I. Rotcher, M.V.: stated that he loves the shuttle and hopes it will continue
  operating in the City. He suggested better advertising and expanding the route so ridership
  will increase.

City Manager Report

City Manager Wilberg announced that he has passed out the monthly report for the Marguerite
Aquatics Complex. Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, discussed
progress on the project.

Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented a budget overview in advance of the
budget workshop which will be held on February 2, 2017.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

16.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell congratulated Mayor Bucknum on the birth of her first grandchild today.
He discussed his recent attendance, with Council Member Kelley, at a League of California Cities
workshop for new Mayors and Council Members. He said it was very helpful in his understanding
of a Council Member’s role and what they should do, can do, and should never do. Council
Member Goodell said that if anyone is interested in the agenda and materials that were presented
at the conference, it is available at www.cacities.org/education-events. He also wished Council
Member Kelley a happy birthday and he noted that with the weekend’s new moon, the Chinese
City Council Minutes  5  January 24, 2017
 New Year will begin. In closing, Council Member Goodell said that he has noticed recently that
some of the City’s dog owners are not doing a very good job of picking up after their pets and he
asked everyone to do a better job in this regard.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she and Mayor Bucknum attended a 100th birthday
celebration for John Grimes at Sunrise Assisted Living last weekend and the band, Forever Young,
preformed. She noted that this is a group of approximately 20 senior citizen musicians who are
extremely talented and she hopes the Community Services division can look into using them at
some City events. Council Member Kelley shared that her electric bill was higher than usual this
month and a notice inside the bill explained that there has been a 10% increase. She also announced
that she and Council member Goodell attended a Proposition 64 workshop on the new cannabis
legalization. She said it is a very complex subject and it will bring some changes to our State and
our community so the information they received was very beneficial. Finally, Council Member
Kelley announced that there is a Social Security workshop in the Saddleback Room at city hall on
January 30 and 31, 2017, and participants must register in advance at www.socialsecurity567.com.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths was absent.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs had no comments.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum provided a verbal report on her attendance at a Southern California Association
of Governments (SCAG) meeting, deferred from item #12, and a report on the Orange County
Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO,) deferred from item #13. She also discussed her
recent trip to Washington D.C. to attend the National Mayor's conference and her personal
experience attending the inauguration of President Donald Trump while she was there.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:17 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Thursday, February 2, 2017, at 9:30 a.m. for a budget
workshop.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 14, 2017
City Council Minutes  6  January 24, 2017
